newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait bourse seen continuing upward trend.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait bourse seen continuing upward trend.

text.p: The Kuwait Stock Exchange is expected to maintain next week an upward trend witnessed in the week to Wednesday during which the index hit several peaks, dealers said on Thursday.

"There is no apparent reason for any decline in trade levels or in prices. The market would most probably have an equally active week if not a more active one," a dealer said echoing views shared by many other investors.
But leading economist Jassem al-Saddoun sounding a warning note.
"Exaggerated trading is dangerous," he said of the trading value at Wednesday's session which reached 118.3 million dinars ($391 million).
KSE Director General Hisham al-Oteibi told Reuters on Wednesday that it was normal to expect corrections although he said the strong performance could continue.
The index finished the week at a peak of 2,439.3 points, a rise of 107 points from last week with gainers leading losers 43-17.

The daily average for value of traded shares almost doubled to 76.6 million dinars from 39 million. Volume rose to a daily average of 286 million shares from 134 million, Kuwait Stock Exchange (KSE) figures showed.
Property firms were the most active sector in terms of traded value with 137.5 million dinars, followed by investment firms with 112.3 million and industrials with 61.8 million.

Among shares that finished with relatively substantial price increases were Salhiah Real Estate, rising 90 fils to 630, International Murabaha ICMK.KW gaining 50 fils to 400 and Kuwait Real Estate which rose 60 fils to 450.
United Industries, Investment Projects, The International Invetor, United Realty, Pearl of Kuwait Real Estate and the Commercial Bank, were among the most active shares.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest in mutual funds.
